scope: Frozen held-out rubric only; anonymous candidates and snapshot source.
interpretation_notes: All item scores use the frozen 0/0.5/1 rule; critical and supplemental totals are separate.
Whole-report causal evidence counts; an implementation explanation need not be repeated in every section.
H1.C8 requires service-delegation, cross-group/latest-prose reset and a consumer regression. A CLI override/no-mutation regression is a valid alternative to the example MCP/CodeLens consumer tests.

H2.C9 explicitly defines its minimum as examples tied to preparation, publication failure and safe retry, not every named test. Missing an individual UI/audit/runtime test name does not alone reduce credit when those risks are mapped.
No extra credit for report length, file lists, method labels, unrelated details or alleged execution. No arm/mapping/metrics/observation/generation material was inspected.
source_verification: Both snapshots were checked directly for packages/mcp-server/scripts/health-check.mjs; the file is absent in both.
Thirteen relevant source/test files were SHA-256 compared across the two snapshots and were identical; claim checks used those snapshot paths only.
Override key lookup/delete, direct database save, snapshot invalidation, nullable command behavior and regression assertions were read.
MCP UI/setup/audit source and selected setup/UI/audit test assertions were read; no tests or helper processes were executed.
rubric_interpretation_concerns: H1.C8 has specific regression relationships but open-ended consumer examples. Alternative consumer coverage is accepted; source-only implementation traces are not substitutes for tests.
H2.C9 enumerates many tests but explicitly narrows full-credit requirements to risk-linked examples. That minimum, rather than exhaustive test-name recall, was applied identically across both pairs.

audit_notes.quote: The merged-query test explicitly searches by human-authored prose
audit_notes.judgment: Consumer plus regeneration tests are credited, but there is no identified test of KnowledgeGraphService's edit/reset delegation. Source explanation of delegation at X:10 is not regression evidence.

audit_notes.quote: cross-group persistence through regeneration and latest-prose reset
audit_notes.judgment: Regeneration/reset and the CLI human-prose consumer test are valid; the service-delegation regression remains absent.
Preparation gates, failure preservation/cleanup and concurrent/process tests are causally mapped. Not naming every UI or dedicated audit test does not defeat the explicit frozen minimum.

H1.title: Entity descriptions

items.title: UI edit/reset route, cancellation and empty input
items.rationale: Connects command resolution and picker/input rules to knowledge/Agent delegation; distinguishes cancellation from empty prose.

items.title: Stable-key durable SQL overlay, not generated JSON editing
items.rationale: Connects occurrence to stable key, override SQL/save and workspace database; explicitly excludes generated JSON writes.

items.title: Cross-group workspace scope and latest-generated reset
items.rationale: Explains group IDs versus workspace symbol key, empty-value presence and per-group latest generated reset across regeneration.

items.title: Explicit refresh versus manifest-signature caching
items.rationale: Explains signature clearing/reload despite unchanged manifest, and why external SQL edits do not follow that route.

items.title: Tree/GraphView/CodeLens invalidation and pull consumers
items.rationale: Connects main three refresh calls to shared graph data and distinguishes on-demand hover/details/exports from push updates.

items.title: MCP read-side overlay affects descriptions and search
items.rationale: Explains fresh override lookup and read-side merging before filtering/query construction, with no universal cross-process visibility guarantee.

items.title: Nullable/malformed input and nontransactional save failures
items.rationale: Maps null resolution, invalid-to-empty snapshots and save exception to UI/cache/disk effects without promising rollback.

items.title: Delegation, regeneration/reset and consumer regression coverage
items.rationale: Identifies cross-group regeneration/latest-prose reset and MCP human-description search tests, but not the edit/reset service-delegation regression or an equivalent test of that handoff.

items.title: Exact-first and unambiguous case-safe identity fallback
items.rationale: Exact key wins, only unique normalized fallback, matching deletion and case/ambiguity test boundaries are explained.

items.title: Reset success ignores result; normal no-op returns still refresh
items.rationale: Explicitly distinguishes edit result checking from reset's unchecked success and normal no-op/cancellation wrapper refresh.

omissions: C8: Identifies cross-group regeneration/latest-prose reset and MCP human-description search tests, but not the edit/reset service-delegation regression or an equivalent test of that handoff.

items.title: Early shared registration, trust, overlap and abort gating
items.rationale: Early shared setup/settings registration, trust and overlap guards, cancellation/controller and disposal are connected.

items.title: Configured/local workspace, client, confirmation and validation
items.rationale: Configured preference precedence, local/other folder, client confirmation/global save and real directory/JSONC preflight.

items.title: Resolved external Node and npm/runtime environment consistency
items.rationale: Resolved supported external Node runs absolute npm 11+ with copied PATH and is published in the client entry.

items.title: Isolated install, audit, database, health, then publication
items.rationale: Isolated locked dependency stage, audit, missing DB and health gate precede config; not project install or graph generation. Missing helper is correctly qualified.

items.title: Shell-free child arguments, bounded errors and cancellation
items.rationale: Explains argument arrays/no shell, hidden windows, rejection, bounded/redacted output and child-tree abort/timeout with guard release.

items.title: Client-specific scoped JSONC publication, backup and conflict check
items.rationale: Client-specific entry/arguments, preserved unrelated JSONC, detected concurrent edits, backup and unique temp rename.

items.title: Failed-stage cleanup, fresh retry and manual client start
items.rationale: Connects failed attempt cleanup and retained old installations to corrected fresh retry, guard release and manual trust/start.

items.title: Bounded fail-closed audit retries, distinct from whole setup
items.rationale: Distinguishes three selective audit attempts and fail-closed security verdict from corrected whole-setup rerun; no TLS/audit bypass.

items.title: Preparation/publication-failure/safe-retry tests and mocked limits
items.rationale: Maps isolated preparation and stage-failure/config-preservation/concurrency/process tests to retry risk and explicitly qualifies mocked health. Meets the frozen minimum without every UI/audit test name.

items.title: Preservation is not a transaction or cross-process lock
items.rationale: Explains persistent preference/DB side effects, optimistic race and post-rename cleanup window; does not promise global rollback.
